name: Diagnostic write-up
summary: Turns a technician's diagnostic notes and photos into a plain write-up of the fault and the work it needs, filed on the job, then queued to the customer for approval. Crons read and draft; a person approves every send.

inspection-write-up.evidence: 2 automotive diagnostic calls were read and described no steps; the steps below come from the three workshop platform pages

covered_by.photos-evidence: draft (counts and names the job photos)

crons.name: intake
crons.summary: Active jobs in Quote status that are waiting for a diagnostic write-up.

crons.name: draft
crons.summary: Write the diagnostic write-up from the technician's notes and photos as a job note marked DRAFT. Parks any job with no usable notes.

crons.name: queue
crons.summary: Queue the write-up email to the customer for approval once the shop has removed the DRAFT marker from the note.

draft_ops_note: Draft operations reach nobody outside the business: reads, and an internal job note. The customer email is a live operation and waits for a person.

servicem8.covers: Quote-status jobs, technician notes, photo list, primary contact, the write-up note, the customer email

gaps: Autoleap, Tekmetric and WorkshopMate: their pages describe a write-up step, but none has operations mapped in the kit, so no adapter is built. Their help pages do not say how a booking or inspection reaches the write-up.
Fergus and AroFlo: the kit maps job notes and attachments for both, but no adapter is built here. Check sign-in and field names against their specs before adding one.
Scan-tool and fault-code readings: no platform in the evidence reads them. The technician types them into the notes, and the write-up only carries what is written there.
Root-cause and recommended-work judgment is an agent-skill step (SKILL.md). Nothing in the crons decides what is wrong with a car.
Photos are counted and named in the note but not attached to the customer email: attaching them needs a live check of the attachment path first.
The calls evidence is thin: 2 of the 3 workflow calls were read, and neither described steps. Re-mine before trusting the step list.
No cron changes a job's status. Moving a job to Work Order on approval stays with the shop.

evidence.calls: 2 calls read of 3 listed for this workflow, 0 rejected, 0 steps described
evidence.platforms: autoleap, tekmetric and workshopmate mapped step by step from their own pages; none has kit operations, so ServiceM8 is the only adapter
